title: Pyramid Featured in STIQ Ltd’s 2026 Controls Report
summary: STIQ Ltd, a publisher of industry reports on supply chain technology and warehouse automation, shared their picking automation report.
body_markdown:
## PLCs aren’t going away anytime soon, but warehouse controls are changing.


STIQ Ltd.’s ([https://www.stiq.ltd](https://www.stiq.ltd/) ) new **Controls 2026** **report** takes an in-depth look at the technologies, engineering strategies and market trends shaping controls for material handling and warehouse automation.


Pyramid is proud to be among the industry experts contributing to the research. Jason Johnson, Vice President of Controls Engineering at Pyramid, shared perspective drawn from Pyramid’s experience designing, integrating, and modernizing controls for automated distribution and fulfillment operations. STIQ interviewed 25 organizations for the report, with a strong focus on system and controls integrators across North America and Europe.


## What’s changing in warehouse controls?


The report explores several important questions facing automation teams today, including:


- Why PLCs remain the dominant controls platform even as IPCs, soft PLCs and software-defined automation gain attention.
- How brownfield modernization and controls retrofits are becoming increasingly important as installed automation ages.
- Why decentralized or cabinetless controls architectures continue to expand across material handling applications.
- How safety PLCs, cybersecurity and new standards are influencing controls design.
- Where simulation, emulation, AI and data-intensive applications may fit into the future controls landscape.
- Whether more open and hardware-agnostic controls architectures will eventually challenge today’s established PLC ecosystems.


The report notes that PLCs remain the default choice for the large majority of integrators surveyed, while emerging technologies are creating new options for applications requiring greater computing power, connectivity and flexibility.


Johnson contributes Pyramid’s perspective throughout the report on topics ranging from modern PLC capabilities and controls modernization to safety technology and decentralized system design. One observation: today’s PLCs have advanced considerably in processing power and capability compared with previous generations.
